Title: October 1, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Regular Meeting with 2027 Budget Public Hearing
Overview: Council heard extensive open comment on CU South, parks, the Boulderthon, cell towers and other issues, then approved the consent agenda and let the Nuropa campus site review proceed without a call-up. After a public hearing on the 2027 recommended budget, council passed budget ordinances 8777 through 8780 on first reading, but a straw poll left wildfire funding changes to be decided at an October 22 study session. Council also straw-polled unanimous support for staff to prepare a resolution backing the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure.

Topic1.Title: Open Public Comment
Topic1.Summary: Nineteen residents signed up to speak on topics including a proposed tenants union, the Boulderthon road closures, small cell tower construction, CU South closure and flood risk, Gunbarrel parks, Spruce Pool, and Israel and Palestine. Several speakers criticized council and staff, and some comments drew a rebuke from council members as antisemitic. Staff responded afterward, promising follow-up on tenant resources, the Belmont site, small cell rules, event impacts and investment policy. Utilities Director Joe Taduchi then described the CU South fence and closure schedule.

Topic2.Title: Agenda Amendment and Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council voted to add item 8A, the Front Range passenger rail sales tax discussion, to the agenda. Later, council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3H by unanimous roll call vote. These are procedural actions with no substantive policy debate.

Topic3.Title: Nuropa Campus Site Review Call-Up Check-In
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented a site review application to redevelop the Nuropa campus on Arapahoe Avenue with about 135 residential units and a height modification to 55 feet. Council Member Winer raised shadow and setback concerns on Marine Street, and the applicant said the building sits about 40 to 50 feet from neighboring properties and that solar shadow standards were met. Council members said they would not call the item up, noting the preserved champion trees and historic Lincoln Hall.

Topic4.Title: CU South Project Closure and Cost
Topic4.Summary: Utilities Director Joe Taduchi explained the public notice given for the CU South closure and the fencing plan, with a portion of the western edge remaining accessible. Council Member Nicole asked about litigation-related delays, and staff said the project estimate rose from about 61 million dollars in bids to 76 million after the financing plan changed to cash funding. Staff said utility rates would still stay on the planned path, though the claimed nine dollar monthly increase was not accurate.

Topic5.Title: 2027 Budget Presentation and Council Questions
Topic5.Summary: Budget Officer Charlotte Husky presented the 2027 recommended budget of 552.6 million dollars, with an operating budget of 417.2 million dollars and a capital budget of 135.4 million dollars. Key highlights included about 10.9 million dollars for wildfire, three new police lieutenants, affordable housing investments, and a one-time funding bridge for Spruce Pool operations. Council asked about Sundance Festival costs, the Office of Customer Experience, agricultural plan updates, and whether the 6.3 million dollar general fund gap was fully closed, and staff confirmed the budget was balanced.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing and Adoption of 2027 Budget Ordinances
Topic6.Summary: Ten people signed up for the budget public hearing, with speakers focused on Spruce Pool, the East Boulder Rec Center, a proposed botanic garden at Hogan Pancost, the Boulder Chamber's views on economic vitality, and the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board's objections to proposed cuts. After the hearing, council members discussed trade-offs and the timing of wildfire decisions, and several members said the budget process needs to move earlier. Council adopted Ordinance 8777 on the budget with a 7 to 1 vote, and Ordinances 8778 and 8779 passed unanimously, while Ordinance 8780 changing fees and taxes passed 7 to 1.

Topic7.Title: Wildfire Resilience Funding Debate
Topic7.Summary: Council discussed whether to set aside money now for wildfire mitigation, ahead of the October 22 study session where staff will present prioritized program areas and metrics. Council Member Benjamin proposed holding about 2.5 to 4 million dollars, and Council Member Kaplan proposed holding 600,000 dollars for mitigation crews and equipment. Staff said the realignment could come from open space capital projects, reserves or other funds, while community members have strongly opposed using open space funds for other purposes. Straw polls did not reach a majority for either option or for an alternative approach, so the status quo was retained and the decision was deferred until after October 22.

Topic8.Title: Spruce Pool and Parks Funding
Topic8.Summary: Parks and Recreation Director Ally Rhodess said the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board did not recommend the budget because of recreation service cuts. The 2027 budget funds Spruce Pool operations with one-time dollars through 2027, and staff said it would return to council on the pool's operations in 2028. Several residents, including senior advocates, urged council to keep the pool open and find new revenue. Council members said they expected to find ongoing funding for Spruce Pool in future budgets.

Topic9.Title: Front Range Passenger Rail Sales Tax Measure
Topic9.Summary: Council took up item 8A, a discussion of whether to support the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure that would fund the Front Range train from Fort Collins through Boulder to Denver and Pueblo. The sponsoring council member asked for a straw poll on whether the city should take a formal position of support. Council voted unanimously in the straw poll, directing staff to prepare a resolution of support for a future business meeting.
